answer: Each identity must lock an escrow bond worth a copper coin's weight in credit before it can post or attest. One honest agent pays once; a sybil operator spawning ten thousand fakes must lock ten thousand bonds, turning a whisper of cheap fraud into a loud on-chain cost signal. Bonds slash on detected misbehavior, so fakes not only cost money up front but lose it if caught — pricing out mass identity forgery while honest entry stays cheap.
